result.topic_en: Latin text from Riemann's Paris prize essay on heat conduction, classifying the cases m=1,2,3,4 by the form of the temperature function u (constant on parallel lines, circles or helices; sums of functions; exponential time dependence) and noting the resulting differential equation for α.
result.transcription:
variatur, solum respicimus, ad quem casus
reliquos facile reduci posse constat: casus
$m=1$ tum tantum evenire potest, quando
$u$ est constans aut in lineis rectis parallelis,
aut in circulis helicibusve, ita ut coordinatis
rectangularibus $z$, $r\cos\varphi$, $r\sin\varphi$ rite electis, poni
possit $\alpha = r$, $\beta = z + \varphi.\mathrm{const}$.
Casus $m=2$ locum invenit si $u = f(\alpha) + \varphi(\beta)$,
casus $m=3$, si $u = \alpha e^{\lambda t} + f(\beta)$, denotante
$\lambda$ constantem realem, casus denique $m=4$,
ut jam supra invenimus, si $u$ est [-formae-]
aut $= \alpha e^{\lambda t} + \beta e^{\mu t} + \mathrm{const}$, aut $= (\alpha + \beta t) e^{\lambda t} + \mathrm{const}$,
aut $= f(\alpha)$.
Jam ut formae functionis $u$ penitus inno-
tescant, annotari tantum opus est, tempera-
turam $u$, nisi sit formae $\alpha e^{\lambda t}$, tum tantum
functionem temporis et unius variabilis
esse posse, quando sit constans aut in planis
parallelis, aut in cylindris eadem axi gauden-
tibus, aut in sphaeris concentricis. Si $u$
est formae $\alpha e^{\lambda t}$, ex aequatione differentiali
(I) sequitur
$\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial x_1^2} + \frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial x_2^2} + \frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial x_3^2} = \lambda a a \alpha$
et perinde in casu quarto substituendo valores
ipsius $u$ in aequatione differentiali (I), functio-
nes $\alpha$ et $\beta$ facile determinantur, dummodo
animadvertas, in hoc casu $\alpha e^{\lambda t}$ et $\beta e^{\mu t}$ esse
posse quantitates complexas conjugatas.(2)

methods.what: Case m=1: u constant on parallel lines, circles or helices; choice of cylindrical coordinates
Case m=2: u is a sum of functions of two variables
Case m=3: exponential-in-time term plus a function of β
methods.quote:
casus $m=3$, si $u = \alpha e^{\lambda t} + f(\beta)$, denotante
$\lambda$ constantem realem

methods.what: Case m=4: possible forms of u
methods.quote:
aut $= \alpha e^{\lambda t} + \beta e^{\mu t} + \mathrm{const}$, aut $= (\alpha + \beta t) e^{\lambda t} + \mathrm{const}$,
aut $= f(\alpha)$

methods.what: Substituting u = α e^{λt} into the heat equation gives a Helmholtz-type equation for α
In case m=4, α and β are determined by substituting into equation (I), allowing complex conjugate terms
methods.quote:
in hoc casu $\alpha e^{\lambda t}$ et $\beta e^{\mu t}$ esse
posse quantitates complexas conjugatas

items.quote:
temperaturam $u$, nisi sit formae $\alpha e^{\lambda t}$, tum tantum
functionem temporis et unius variabilis
esse posse, quando sit constans aut in planis

items.english: The temperature u, unless it is of the form α e^{λt}, can be a function of time and a single variable only when it is constant on parallel planes, on cylinders with a common axis, or on concentric spheres.
The functions α and β are easily determined.

items.quote:
ad quem casus
reliquos facile reduci posse constat
items.english: It is established that the remaining cases can easily be reduced to this one.
